text: hey everybody I spent most of my teenage years in Colorado I went to high school in a little town called Niwot I got
kicked out of the University of Northern Colorado after a single semester I was there in 97 I was there in 98 and
something that would not be unusual to hear me say is that there's only one real football team in the NFL and that
the Raiders were nothing and less than nothing and they didn't matter and anyone who heard me say that would know exactly what I was talking about I
was not actually denying the existence of an NFL team called the Raiders I was not actually denying that they had any
relevance whatsoever I was rhetorically denigrating them and this is the exact same kind of rhetoric that we find in
the Bible regarding the other gods see there's no monotheism anywhere in the Bible every last author of the biblical text acknowledged the reality the
existence of other gods but they rhetorically denigrated them demonize them and marginalized them and in some places it went so far as to say Well
they're nothing they're less than nothing and then we have the god of Israel saying I am and there is no other
none of this is an actual conscious intentional philosophical rejection of the existence of the other gods it is
only rejecting their importance their power their relevance to the people of Israel we have the exact same rhetoric
by the same authors being directed at the larger and more powerful Empires around Israel we have the Assyrians being called nothing and less than
nothing we have uh Nineveh and Moab and Babylon personified and then the authors are putting into their mouth the exact
same claim that we have the god of Israel making I am and there is no other that is not the personified Babylon saying I'm the only city that exists and
no other cities actually exist it is rhetoric that is denying the relevance the power the importance of the other
cities for my people I am the only one that matters that's what that rhetoric is intended to mean because alongside it
you also have references to the Divine counsel and other Divine beings so there's no monotheism anywhere in the
Bible at all and I'm actually going to be participating in a conference with 11 other Scholars at Brown University uh in
May of next year called the meanings and ends of monotheism and we are going to be discussing why the concept of
monotheism is not a useful analytical framework for looking at the Bible or even at late Antiquity that it is a philosophical
development of a much later time
